title: The Woman Who Survived the Titanic and Both Its Sisters
notes: Register: dry, almost amused, as she wrote about it herself. High energy and comic timing for her life and work; the Titanic section (s26-s35) is the only place the tone and the motion drop.
Retitled from 'The Woman Who Survived Three Ship Sinkings': the Olympic did not sink.
A public-domain photograph of Violet Jessop exists (p05) and is used three times. Elsewhere she is a cartoon with a vague face; her real face appears only in that photograph.

Nothing about the disasters is generated: no iceberg, no sinking, no lifeboat, no propellers, no figures on a sinking deck. The Hawke collision is tokens on a map; the Titanic and Britannic nights are real photographs, empty sea and dark fields. At s28 Violet holds the baby on a plain dark field: no boat, no water.

p12 is a real photograph of Titanic's lifeboats taken from the Carpathia. Do not caption or label it as lifeboat 16; nobody can identify which boat it is. It is a WebP file: convert to PNG before compositing.
Every ship photograph is a real period image, all public domain except the restored Britannic-and-Olympic photograph (p07, CC BY-SA 4.0).
LOW RESOLUTION: p06 and p12 are small. Show them as cards at native size.
Every archival URL was resolved from the Commons API.
Guide object: the toothbrush (s03, s34, s41, s58).

violet.desc: Violet Jessop: as a young Edwardian stewardess in a black dress, white apron and cap; as a First World War nurse in a pale VAD uniform with a red cross; as a girl; and in old age in a cardigan; slim, dark-haired, simple vague face, brisk and capable posture

mother.desc: Violet's mother Katherine, an Irish woman of the 1900s in a stewardess's black dress and apron, simple vague face

editor.desc: a memoir editor of the 1990s in a tweed jacket with a notebook, simple vague face

crowd.desc: extras: eight small Edwardian children, Edwardian lady passengers ringing for service, a woman in a long coat on a ship's deck, convalescent soldiers in hospital blues, simple vague faces
